newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-GASCOIGNE'S FUTURE AT RANGERS IN DOUBT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GASCOIGNE'S FUTURE AT RANGERS IN DOUBT.

text.p: Paul Gascoigne's trouble-strewn two-year stay at Glasgow Rangers could be drawing to a close, if stinging new criticism from his manager, Walter Smith, is an accurate barometer of the club's feelings.
The controversial England star's future at the Scottish champions is now in grave doubt after Smith admitted he may have made a mistake in bringing Gazza to Ibrox.
Gascoigne's litany of bad publicity for his off-field behaviour has forced Smith to question his decision in paying 4.2 million pounds ($6.9 million) to Lazio for the wayward midfielder in 1995.

It has heightened speculation the former Newcastle and Tottenham player could now be offloaded in the summer. A return to England seems most likely, with Derby and Sunderland - who made an inquiry six months ago - among the interested parties.

Rangers have been embarrassed by the player's confession he beat up his wife Sheryl just months after marrying and recent pictures of him trawling New York bars with TV celebrity Chris Evans while he was supposed to be recuperating from injury.

Smith admitted yesterday: "I was the person responsible for bringing him here. His actions have tarnished the club's and my own image a great deal and it's been a very unpleasant side for me to handle.
"When I signed him, I was 100 per cent clear about my judgement but the percentage drops with every incident that happens.

"So does the level of backing from the club. The on-field part has been a pleasing part of him coming to Rangers and he's been successful to a certain degree. But other parts, away from the pitch, have made me seriously question my own judgement in bringing him here"
Of the wife-beating incident, Smith said simply: "Paul Gascoigne knows that Rangers Football Club were totally unhappy at what happened there."
Gascoigne's 19 goals last season helped Rangers to the Scottish title and this season they are set to win another, their ninth successive championship, although injury has limited his contribution.

He has also been unable to make a significant contribution in Europe. Injury meant Rangers could not use him in key Champions league games, added to which he was sent off twice; against Borussia Dortmund last season and against Ajax this season.

Smith, in Monaco to watch tonight's UEFA Cup semifinal with Inter Milan, reportedly has as interest in the home club's Patrick Blondeau and Emmanuel Petit as well as Inter's veteran defender, Guiseppe Bergomi.
